notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0562.tlg001.perseus-: Baccheius, Tandasis and Marcianus are teachers not otherwise identified; the name Tandasis may be corrupt.

nodes.text: From Diognetus: not to be zealous about trifles; and to disbelieve what is said by wonder-mongers and sorcerers about incantations and the sending away of *daimones* [spirits] and such things; and not to keep quails [for fighting], nor to be excited about such things; and to put up with frank speech; and to become at home with philosophy, and to hear first Baccheius, then Tandasis and Marcianus; and to write dialogues as a boy; and to desire the camp-bed and the skin, and whatever else of that kind belongs to the Greek training.
